title: Daycare Preschool Office Compliance Fees: Insurance, Security, and Sanitation Add-Ons in Janitorial Bids
seoTitle: Daycare Preschool Office Compliance Fees: Insurance & Sanitation Add-Ons
metaDescription: Daycare preschool office compliance fees often add 10–28% to cleaning bids. See costs for checks, COI limits, and safer disinfectants, then compare quotes.
excerpt: Child care licensing, background check rules, insurance requirements, and safer-chemical expectations all raise the cost of cleaning a daycare or preschool admin suite. This guide prices each add-on and shows how to keep requirements tight without paying for services you do not need.
quickAnswer: Compliance and sanitation add-ons typically raise a daycare or preschool admin cleaning bid by 10 to 28 percent, or about $20 to $65 per visit on a 1,400 sq ft suite cleaned daily, roughly $430 to $1,410 per month at 21.65 visits. The main drivers are fingerprint-based background checks and assigned crews, higher insurance and bonding, EPA-registered disinfectants with fast dwell times plus Safer Choice general cleaners, and restricted after-hours access windows.

blocks.text: Why Daycare Admin Bids Carry a Compliance Premium

A child care center's admin suite looks like a small office, but the vendor cleaning it inherits obligations that most office accounts never carry. State child care licensing rules govern who may access the building and how surfaces are sanitized. Landlords and franchisors set insurance minimums. Accreditation programs and parents expect fragrance-free, low-VOC products. And because the building is occupied from early morning to evening, cleaning windows are narrow. Each of those constraints costs the vendor money, and a well-written bid shows you where.

The baseline for an admin suite under 2,500 sq ft is $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit, and $0.09 to $0.15 for 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, with restrooms at $15 to $30 each per visit. A 1,400 sq ft suite on LVT (1.04 multiplier) cleaned daily (0.9 multiplier) with one restroom runs about $172 to $292 per visit before compliance add-ons. The sections below price what sits on top.

blocks.title: Insurance terms specific to child care
blocks.text: Beyond general liability commonly set at $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate, many child care operators and their insurers ask vendors to carry abuse and molestation coverage or confirm it is not excluded. Fewer janitorial firms carry it, which narrows the bidder pool and nudges prices up. Confirm the requirement with your own carrier before making it mandatory.
Background Checks, Access Control, and Security Add-Ons

Most states require background checks for anyone who may have unsupervised contact with children, and many operators extend the rule to all vendors with keys, even if they only work after closing. Fingerprint-based checks take longer and cost more than name-based screening, and vendors must keep a bench of cleared substitutes, which is why they price the requirement into every visit rather than as a one-time fee.

items: Require a named, background-cleared primary cleaner and at least one cleared backup.
Prohibit uncleared substitutes from entering; the vendor skips and credits the visit instead.
Issue individual alarm codes and keys or fobs, logged by worker, and revoke them on the day of separation.
Set a hard exit time at least 60 minutes before the first staff arrival so cleaning never overlaps child drop-off.
Include a re-key clause stating the vendor pays for lock changes caused by lost keys.
Keep photo ID badges visible during every visit, including early-morning restock runs.

blocks.text: Disinfection and Safer Chemistry in a Child Care Building

Daycare admin areas need a two-product approach. General surfaces, floors, and glass should be cleaned with a low-odor, plant-based or Safer Choice product. High-touch points, restroom fixtures, and changing tables need an EPA-registered disinfectant used at the right dilution and left wet for the label contact time, and then allowed to dry fully well before children arrive.

ECOS Pro Orange Plus all-purpose cleaner is an EPA Safer Choice, plant-derived neutral cleaner in a 1-gallon jug with low VOC content, suitable for lobby counters, office furniture, and walls. Diversey Virex II 256 is a one-step neutral pH quaternary disinfectant that dilutes at 1:256, giving a low cost per use for restroom fixtures, door hardware, and hard floors, but the crew must honor its dwell time and ensure the product is dry and residue-free on surfaces children might touch. Where the lobby or director's office has engineered or hardwood floors, Bona Pro Series commercial hardwood floor cleaner is GREENGUARD Gold certified and leaves no residue, protecting urethane finishes better than mopping wood with a disinfectant solution.

blocks.title: Do not let disinfectant replace cleaning
blocks.text: Disinfectants work on pre-cleaned surfaces. A crew that sprays a soiled changing table and wipes immediately has neither cleaned nor disinfected it. Your scope should require a clean step, then disinfectant applied and left wet for the full label dwell time.

Vendors working in child care buildings carry documentation overhead. OSHA Hazard Communication requires trained workers and Safety Data Sheets for every product on site. Changing tables and bodily fluid incidents bring the bloodborne pathogens standard into play, which means PPE, training, and an exposure control plan. Licensing inspectors may ask what chemicals are stored in the building and where, so the vendor must keep products in locked closets out of children's reach. Expect bidders who handle this well to be slightly more expensive and much less risky.

items.name: Request a compliance packet with every bid
items.text: COI, bond certificate, background check policy, Hazard Communication program, bloodborne pathogens training records, and a product list with EPA registration numbers.

items.name: Separate compliance lines from base pricing
items.text: Ask vendors to show base cleaning, restrooms, add-ons, and compliance costs as separate lines so you can compare like for like.

items.name: Confirm chemical storage
items.text: Designate a locked janitorial closet and require the vendor to keep all concentrates and spray bottles there, labeled per HazCom.

items.name: Set an incident response fee
items.text: Agree a flat call-out price for bodily fluid cleanup or a sick-child event so it is not billed at an open-ended $55 to $95 per hour specialty rate.

items.name: Audit quarterly
items.text: Spot check badges, product labels, and dwell-time practice each quarter, and update the packet when the vendor changes staff or products.

blocks.text: Some requirements are essential: background-cleared staff, correct insurance, EPA-registered disinfection, and secure chemical storage. Others are often oversold, such as nightly electrostatic spraying of the whole admin suite or fogging offices that no child enters. Pay for what licensing, your insurer, and your franchisor actually require, and spend the remainder on daily attention to the lobby, entry, and restrooms where parents form their impression.

faqs.q: Are background checks for cleaning crews legally required in daycare centers?
faqs.a: Rules vary by state. Many states require checks for anyone with potential unsupervised access to children, and licensing staff may interpret that to include vendors holding keys. Even where it is not strictly required after hours, most operators and insurers treat it as a condition of contract, so expect it in every competitive bid.

faqs.q: How do I budget compliance costs for daily cleaning?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-visit compliance amount by 21.65, the number of weekday visits in a 4.33-week average month. A $40 per-visit compliance layer equals about $866 per month. Keep it as a separate invoice line so you can adjust it if requirements change.

faqs.q: Can a daycare admin suite use green products only?
faqs.a: General cleaning can use Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice products, and many child care programs prefer fragrance-free options. Disinfection of restrooms, changing tables, and door hardware still requires an EPA-registered disinfectant used according to the label, so the scope should list both product types.

faqs.q: What happens if the vendor sends an uncleared substitute?
faqs.a: Your contract should state that uncleared workers may not enter and that missed visits are credited. Some operators also add a liquidated damages clause or treat repeated violations as grounds for termination without penalty.

faqs.q: Which compliance-related services are usually excluded?
faqs.a: Outbreak response disinfection, electrostatic spraying, classroom toy sanitizing, carpet extraction, and post-inspection deep cleans are typically excluded from base pricing. Price them as on-call services with a defined per-sq-ft or flat rate so you can authorize them quickly when needed.
